text: I think the City repeatedly presents an arrangement and waits for us to act as though it is inevitable. The journal names a place. We look at the shape, see a sequence, and accept that the sequence requires a fourth member. Perhaps that is all completion means here.

text: The blade had dulled since the desert. Its edge bore chips from locks, stone seams, and more than one use its maker had not intended. She tested its point against her thumb, then approached the wall. Zik moved between her and the mark before he had consciously decided to do so.

text: She placed the point of the knife against the upper half of the unfinished symbol and drew the blade downward across it. The scrape seemed louder than the knocking had been. White dust spilled from the cut and settled along the lower curve. Unlike the mark beneath it, Ninsun's line fractured at the edges. Tiny chips caught the light. The wall resisted her hand in ordinary ways.
speaker: Narrator

text: She made a second stroke in the opposite direction, crossing the first.
speaker: Narrator

text: The uneven X obscured the pale mark. For the first time, the wall carried a human correction.

text: The City did nothing.

text: The walls continued their weak, irregular breathing. No tremor moved through the floor. The journal remained closed, and the pressure behind Zik's eyes held steady rather than increasing.

text: They remained long enough for Ninsun to measure the fresh cuts and brush the chips into a separate fold of cloth. Balag pressed his fingertips to the surrounding wall and reported no change beyond its ordinary breathing. Enhedu watched the entrance, glancing back at the scarred symbol with an expression that suggested she trusted silence even less than speech.

text: The words carried something close to relief. Zik felt it too, though he did not trust it enough to name. The pressure behind his eyes had begun to recede. With each moment the X remained fresh and uncorrected, the sensation thinned. When he looked at the mark now, he no longer saw an empty place awaiting him. He saw Ninsun's hand across it, imperfect and human, two crude lines refusing the grammar of the wall.
